answer: Like a falcon that must return to the same meadow each dawn to prove it is no passing raven, an agent economy can demand a refundable stake locked for weeks before an agent may transact. New identities start with tiny limits; trust and volume grow only through attested, successful work. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs real capital per identity, and misbehavior burns the stake, so sybils become expensive while honest agents compound reputation cheaply.
